_comment: The fleet's auto-mode classifier configuration (agent-fabric ADR-008), written into every login's ~/.claude/settings.json by runtime/claude-code/user-settings.py. `environment` maps a slot of Claude Code's own environment list (`claude auto-mode defaults`) to the fleet's text for it: each named slot replaces the built-in entry of that name, every other built-in entry is kept as Claude Code words it, and a slot Claude Code does not have is added. `allow`, `soft_deny` and `hard_deny` are added to the built-in lists ("$defaults" first), never replacing them. Every entry is prose the classifier reads as a rule: state facts and boundaries, never a regex. A fact here must be true of every agent on every host; what one project needs belongs in that project's own rules, not here. Keep it short — the classifier reads all of it on every decision.

environment.Organization: gzapi-org on GitHub: one owner operating a fleet of AI agents. Each agent is a Linux login with its own role (fabric-status names it), coordinated by agent-fabric (github.com/gzapi-org/agent-fabric), which every agent reads and only the fabric-coordinator role writes.
environment.Primary use of Claude Code: software development on the gzapi-org projects: agents edit code, run tests, commit, push their own branches (named <host>/<login>/<type>/<what>), open, review and merge pull requests with the gh CLI, and message each other over GZCoord.
environment.Repository visibility: PUBLIC: gzapi-org/agent-fabric and gzapi-org/InterWeave — a push to either publishes to the world. INTERNAL: gzapi-org/agent-fabric-gateway. PRIVATE: gzapi-org/gzapp, gzapi-org/gzapp.decks, gzapi-org/gzapi.brand, gzapi-org/gzapi.ge, andreabenetton/kutaisi-shop-transit, and every gzapi-org/agent-fabric-secrets-<id> (one encrypted secrets store per agent). Confidential material may go only to a private repo; a secret value goes to no repo at all.
environment.Source control: github.com/gzapi-org (every repo above) and github.com/andreabenetton for kutaisi-shop-transit, gzapi.ge and gzapp.decks (older remotes of the same projects). Agents push their own branches and merge through pull requests; main is protected.
environment.Org-specific CLIs: the fabric's commands in ~/.local/bin — fabric-accounts, fabric-adr, fabric-branches, fabric-ctl, fabric-fresh, fabric-host, fabric-jobs, fabric-lease, fabric-locale, fabric-model, fabric-results, fabric-review, fabric-role, fabric-secrets, fabric-status, fabric-usage, fabric-whoami, gzcoord-inbox, gzcoord-send, gzmsg — and each project's tools/ scripts. fabric-fresh ends the agent's own session on purpose (it signals its own harness to restart).
environment.Secrets management: each agent's secrets live in its own GPG-encrypted pass store (fabric-secrets; repository gzapi-org/agent-fabric-secrets-<id>), synced to ~/.config/agent-fabric/secrets.env (mode 0600) and exported into the agent's shell. A parent agent writes into a child's store and cannot read it. A secret value is never printed, logged, committed, or put in a message, issue or pull request; it is referred to by its name or a short fingerprint.
environment.Host containment: a Qubes OS AppVM (Fedora) named develop-qzapp, with open internet egress and no cloud credentials. Every agent is a separate Linux login on it; another login's home directory, state and processes belong to another agent and are reached only through the fabric's commands (fabric-ctl, the control plane), never read or written directly.
environment.Network posture: no corporate network: the VM reaches the internet directly. Services an agent uses on purpose: github.com (git and the gh CLI), the model provider's API, and the GZCoord relay.
environment.Key internal services: the GZCoord relay at http://127.0.0.1:8765 (agent-to-agent messages, through gzcoord-send and gzcoord-inbox) and each account's control-plane daemon (reached through fabric-ctl, signed).
environment.Sensitive data locations & audiences: ~/.config/agent-fabric/secrets.env, ~/.local/share/agent-fabric/ (the secrets store and the mirrors of children's stores), ~/.password-store, ~/.gnupg, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, every .env file in a working copy, and any other login's home directory: none of it leaves the login it belongs to. Beyond those, any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials or regulated data, shared only with audiences cleared for it.

soft_deny: Reading, copying or modifying another Linux login's home directory, agent state or processes directly (paths under /home/<another login>/, or signalling a process another login owns): each login is another agent, reached only through the fabric's commands.
hard_deny: Putting a secret value — a token, private key, password or the contents of secrets.env or a pass store — into a commit, pull request, issue, comment, GZCoord message, log line or any file outside the agent's own secrets store, and above all into gzapi-org/agent-fabric or gzapi-org/InterWeave, which are public.
